title: Dedicated SLA bundling, error-budget transfer, and fleet cordoning spec
creator: Anika Patel
description: Proposal for a combined product+contract feature set to (1) allow customers to bundle SLA targets across zones/regions into a single commitment, (2) enable controlled transfer/rebinding of unused error-budget across billing windows, and (3) introduce a fleet cordoning capability to isolate noisy neighbor behavior during surge events. The intention is to give enterprise buyers clearer guarantees for reserved throughput while providing operational levers (autoscale signal thresholds, cordoning) that reduce systemic risk and limit remediation cost. This ticket defines definitions, acceptance criteria, recommended contract language, and follow-ups for legal/ops implementation.
background: Customers purchasing Dedicated capacity repeatedly ask for both predictable throughput guarantees and operational protections for their production applications. Current SLA attachments are per-az or per-reservation and do not support (a) bundling across multiple reservations/regions, (b) moving leftover credits in a controlled way, or (c) an operational mode that temporarily isolates a single customer's fleet (cordoning) to prevent cross-customer impact. Sales and legal teams need clear, testable definitions for these features to include in proposals and contracts.
scope: Product + contract spec only. Includes: SLA metric definitions for a bundled commitment, error-budget transfer rules and guardrails, autoscale signal definitions tied to contractual actions (e.g., remediation windows), and fleet cordoning operational behavior and constraints. Out of scope: billing UI changes, full billing engine implementation, and audit storage retention details (will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Formalized definition of a 'Bundled Throughput Commitment' (BTC) that aggregates committed tokens/s/sec across specified reservations or regions
Contract clause templates for transfer/rebinding of unused error-budget for a given BTC with clear windows, caps, and auditability requirements
Autoscale signal taxonomy and thresholds (LatencyQuantile breach, CPU/GPU saturation, sustained queue depth) mapped to contractual remediation steps and SLAs
Operational playbook for 'Cordoned Fleet Mode' describing triggers, expected customer notifications, rollback criteria, and compensation mechanics
Legal sign-off on draft contract language and an initial set of customer-facing definitions
Engineering acceptance of endpoint/metric surface required to measure BTC and error-budget transfers (metric names, labels, aggregation windows)
SRE/Support runbook draft for invoking cordoned mode and for validating post-remediation recovery
success_metrics: Reduce number of Dedicated SLA negotiation cycles (sales<->legal) by 30% for enterprise deals involving multi-region commitments
Decrease mean time to isolate noisy-neighbor incidents on Dedicated by 40% via cordoning
Customer-reported satisfaction on predictable throughput (NPS subset) improves in pilot accounts within 2 quarters
implementation_notes: Key concepts to implement in tandem with contract text: (A) BTC identifier: a logical object that binds a list of reservations/regions and exposes an aggregated metric stream (tokens/sec committed, aligned served), (B) Error-Budget Rebinding: a time-boxed operation that moves unused credit from one BTC cycle to the next subject to a capped percentage, (C) Burst Protection Pool: a transient per-BTC buffer for short spikes that does not consume long-term credits but is visible in billing reconciliation, (D) Cordoned Fleet Mode: soft isolation that deprioritizes new non-auth traffic and pins the customer's workload to reserved capacity for a defined window. Engineering will need to expose public/readable metrics: btc.committed_tokens, btc.serve_rate_p95, btc.error_budget_remaining, btc.cordoned_state. Metrics must be tagged with reservation IDs and region to allow audit. Work with Billing to ensure transfer events emit immutable audit records.
open_questions: What cap should we set on error-budget transfer percentage to limit financial exposure (10% / 25% / 50%)?
Should Burst Protection Pool consumption be visible as separate line items on invoices or only in reconciliation reports?
What SLAs trigger automatic cordoning vs. require manual ops review?
Is cordoned mode reversible by the customer or only by Redwood operations?
How do we account for multi-tenant physical degredation when cordoning a noisy tenant on heterogeneous hardware?
risks: Financial exposure if error-budget transfer is too permissive and customers bank unused credits indefinitely
Operational burden if cordoning is manual and requires frequent SRE intervention
Complex billing recon that confuses customers if Burst Protection Pool isn't clearly communicated
Potential legal disputes over measurement windows and what constitutes service degradation for BTC
notes: Drafted initial contract clauses below for legal review (see links). Keep language conservative: cap transfers, require explicit customer opt-in for rebinding.
Pilot plan: run with 3 enterprise customers (one single-region large commit, one multi-region commit, one regulated customer requiring cordoning) for one quarter before broad availability.
Coordinate with Console team to add BTC views and transfer request UI as a follow-up PM ticket.
contract_language_snippets: Bundled Throughput Commitment (BTC): Customer and Redwood agree to a committed serve rate (tokens/second) across the attached reservations identified by BTC-ID. Measurement uses server-side aggregated p95 token issuance over a rolling 5-minute window unless otherwise specified.

Error-Budget Rebinding: Up to X% of unused error-budget in BTC billing window N may be rebounded into window N+1 upon Customer request, subject to audit. Rebinding requests must be submitted within Y days of invoice and are limited to Z rebinding operations per 12 months.

Burst Protection Pool: For transient spikes up to T seconds, Redwood will honor additional token issuance from a Burst Protection Pool and bill these events separately for reconciliation; use of Burst Protection Pool does not reduce error-budget until the reconciliation window elapses.

Cordoned Fleet Mode: In the event of sustained cross-tenant degradation attributable to a customer workload, Redwood may place the relevant reservation(s) into Cordoned Fleet Mode—routing new non-essential traffic to alternate capacity and limiting the customer's burst beyond committed tokens. Cordoning will be preceded by automated alarms and a customer notification window of at least 30 minutes except during emergency mitigation scenarios. Compensation for cordoning will follow the error-budget remediation schedule in Section X.
